text:
marta: quick follow-up from the obs sync 1: batch-enrich vs stream-enrich for cost attribution. want to pick an experiment and owners.

tina: gist: batch-enrich (post-write job) is simpler, keeps runtime fast, but causes delayed/missing attribution for short-lived traces. stream-enrich (ingest-time) gives accurate billing keys at router but increases ingest latency and CPU.

rafael: numbers i ran: stream-enrich adds ~1.6ms median p95 ~+4ms on our hot path and ~7% CPU at peak. batch-enrich backfill gets us ~96% attribution coverage within 30s, 99.7% within 24h.

omar: risk: for chargeback we need high accuracy within minutes. delayed backfill is OK for internal metrics but not for quota enforcement at ingress. which usecases require synchronous attribution?

marta: quota enforcement and real-time billing alerts need sync. analytics, dashboards can tolerate minutes delay. so maybe hybrid: attempt stream-enrich for traffic where sdk supplies attrs; fall back to batch-enrich for missing keys.

tina: hybrid sounds good. operationally we need a cheap fingerprint to detect candidate messages for stream-enrich (sample by route or tenant tier). also need metrics: `ingest.enrich.mode` (stream|batch|fallback) and `ingest.enrich.latency`.

rafael: implementation notes: (1) extend edge to accept optional `X-RW-Attrs` header for immediate usage, (2) enqueue an enrichment token for messages missing it; backfill job dedupes using trace id; (3) add alert if `enrich.fallback_rate` > 0.5% for >10m in production.

omar: SDKs must avoid adding PII. add a validator in proxy + linter rule in SDK repo. Also TTL semantics: sync attrs expire after 5m to avoid stale chargebacks.

ingest-bot: telemetry snapshot: sample-rate=0.02 -> current_stream_attr_presence=0.72, batch_backfill_30s=0.95, avg_ingest_cpu_inc_stream=6.8%

marta: owners: tina (edge shim + metrics), rafael (perf spike + backfill job), omar (SDK linter), i'll coordinate rollout. next step: tina open PR for header schema and canary with 5% traffic. reconvene Thu 11am PT. :thumbsup:
